content:
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by 2–5% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day post-spike.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is rising steadily, true outcome often reverses mid-horizon; add a “reversion buffer” to forecast midpoints.
- When sentiment is low and price drops sharply, model often fails to anticipate further decline; add a “downtrend extension” rule: if true price drops >2% from prior day, forecast should drop 1–2% more.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “late-stage lag”: true outcome often diverges from forecast after day 15–20; apply a “late-stage decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day after day 15.
